title: Named Non-Owner Policy Return Premium and Refund Conventions
content:
## Retention on a named insured's cancellation request

The insured-cancellation retention percentage is the percent of the unearned premium retained on a named-insured cancellation request; a figure of 0.0 means the return is pro rata.

| Package | Insured-cancellation retention percentage |
|---|---|
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner Minimum Limits | 10.0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner Minimum Limits with UM | 10.0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 50/100/50 | 10.0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 100/200/50 | 10.0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 100/300/50 | 10.0 |
| Cardinal Point Non-Owner 250/500/100 | 0.0 |

Current basis for the return on a Named Non-Owner Policy cancellation: the return on a cancellation at the named insured's request is the requested-cancellation unearned premium reduced by the requested-cancellation retention percentage of itself, and fees are not returned; for a nonpayment, underwriting or conversion cancellation the unearned premium is still computed transaction by transaction exactly as for the Owner Auto Policy, each premium-written and additional-premium entry multiplied by the days from the cancellation effective date to expiration and divided by that entry's recorded days (the term's days for premium written), less the same share of earlier returns, with no retention, and a term voided from inception still returns everything written.

## Conventions common to every package

| Convention | Value |
|---|---|
| Return method when the term is replaced by a Cardinal Point Owner Auto Policy | pro rata, with no short-rate retention |
| Cancellation date used when the term is replaced by an Owner Auto Policy | the effective date of the replacing owner term |
| Refund timing | unearned premium is credited to the billing plan within 15 calendar days after the cancellation |
| Day count for pro rata arithmetic | actual calendar days from the effective date to the expiration date |
| Rounding of every premium or refund | to the nearest cent, half up |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A term running from 1 May to 1 November counts 184 days, the actual calendar days from the effective date to the expiration date. A computed refund of 41.235 is credited as 41.24, and one of 41.2349 as 41.23.
